subject: Discovery recap + streaming eval plan and model recommendations
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + streaming model recommendations and next steps

Hi Anya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and the proposed evaluation path so we can validate model fit and address the streaming UX issues you called out.

What we heard (prioritized):
- Primary goal: replace current LLM layer for short chat replies (support triage) with predictable latency and fewer mid-sentence cutoffs/hallucinations.
- Latency target: sub-300ms perceived response time for ~40–80 token replies (you noted 300ms is a hard requirement for UX).
- Quality concerns: partial outputs that end mid-thought, stop-sequence misses, and occasional incoherent token fragments when streaming.
- Data: you can share a redacted sample of typical prompts + expected/acceptable outputs (N≈1k to 5k).

Recommended short-list for evaluation (streaming-first):
- rwd-7b-q4f16 (quantized): best cost/latency balance for short-turn chat with streaming.
- rwd-13b-v2 (fp16): better coherence on longer context; use as fallback for more complex prompts.
- rwd-lite-chat-3b: baseline to validate prompt engineering improvements before moving to bigger models.

Streaming UX mitigations we'll test in the eval:
- Deterministic stop-token sequence with both tokenizer-based and string-match checks (reduces missed stops).
- Chunked streaming: buffer small batches of tokens (e.g., 4–8 tokens) before flush to reduce mid-thought truncation artifacts.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context to lower latency while keeping full decoding behavior.
- Early termination heuristics: detect probable sentence/phrase ends using a light classifier to avoid stopping mid-sentence.

Proposed evaluation plan (attach: mutual_action_plan.xlsx):
1) You provide a 1k sample prompt set + success criteria (we included a prompt_set_v1.jsonl template).
2) Redwood runs a 24–72 hour benchmark across the 3 candidate models using your data. We'll record per-token latency, first-byte latency, streaming burst behaviour, and stop-sequence accuracy.
3) We deliver a benchmark CSV + qualitative examples (sentinel_bench_template.csv + highlights).
4) If results meet your latency and quality SLOs, we run a limited canary (10% traffic) on Dedicated for 7 days.

Immediate asks from you:
- Share the sample prompt set (redacted).
- Confirm the latency SLO: you said 300ms for 40–80 token replies — confirm whether that is p50 or p95.
- Let us know whether we can run the tests against a staging endpoint in your VPC or if you prefer hosted tests.

Attachments included: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MMP), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (template), sentinel_bench_template.csv (metrics schema).

I'll follow up with a technical deep-dive invite for engineering. If that works, Vivek and Dylan will lead the bench and streaming tuning.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for responses in the 40–80 token range. p50 can be lower but p95 is the one that matters for UX.
- Data: attaching a redacted sample (we'll upload the full set to the Drive link you provided). The sample includes short support prompts and a few longer clarifying prompts.
- Staging: we prefer Redwood-hosted test run first to iterate quickly; if we get good results we'll move to a VPC canary.

Stop-sequence and partial output: this is our top pain point today. When agents hit a longer template, the stream sometimes cuts a clause and resumes with unrelated tokens — which looks like a hallucination. We're hoping the deterministic-stop + chunked streaming approach helps.

I've added a procurement contact, Marco (marco.torres@sentinel.ai), to the thread in case we need contract/PO discussions early.

Available for a technical deep-dive Thurs or Fri (your time zone). Also, is there a short checklist we should run on our side before you begin the hosted bench?

Thanks,

Hi Anya —

Thanks — quick technical notes and a minimal config we'll use for the hosted bench. High-level: we want to reproduce the "partial output" locally first, then iterate on decode/flush rules.

Bench config (initial):
- Models: rwd-7b-q4f16 (primary), rwd-13b-v2 (fallback), rwd-lite-chat-3b (baseline)
- max_new_tokens: 80
- temperature: 0.2 (quality-sensitive), top_p: 0.95
- stream_flush_interval_ms: 60 (initial), adjust down to 30ms if tokenization + network allows
- stop_sequences: ["
User:", "
System:", "<END_OF_RESPONSE>"] -- we will use tokenizer-level detection plus string-scan as fallback
- early_termination_threshold: classifier probability > 0.92 (we'll tune)

Prompt-level guardrails (we'll apply to prompt_set_v1.jsonl):
- Ensure every prompt ends with an explicit instruction to finish (e.g., "Respond concisely and end with <END_OF_RESPONSE>").
- Remove ambiguous partial-template tokens (we'll mark candidates in the dataset).

Quick results from a 30-min smoke run on your sample (attached as partial CSV):
- rwd-7b-q4f16: p95 first-byte latency 240ms, mean per-token ~18ms, stop-sequence accuracy 93% on the sample
- rwd-13b-v2: p95 first-byte 360ms (misses your p95 target), stop-sequence accuracy 97%

Immediate proposal: we run the full hosted 24–72h bench once you confirm:
- Acceptance criteria: p95 first-byte < 300ms AND stop-sequence accuracy >= 95% for the short-turn set.
- Deliverables: per-model CSV, example transcripts with raw stream logs, recommended streaming config.

If we don't meet both criteria for rwd-7b-q4f16, we can test a tuned rwd-7b variant with altered kv/cache and a more conservative flush interval before recommending 13b.

Next steps: Karthik — can you confirm the scheduled deep-dive? I'm proposing Thu 2026-08-06 10:00 PT (30–45m). I'll bring the bench logs and a short demo of flush interval changes.

-Vivek
